name: Dimension-Five Critical-Pair Census Through Nine Deletions
statement: Fix the endpoint pair $\{0^5,1^5\}$ in $Q_5$ and quotient deleted subsets of the other thirty vertices by the order-$240$ setwise stabilizer. Through nine deletions, the exhaustive computation covers $22{,}964{,}086$ labelled deletion sets in $106{,}312$ orbits. The numbers of critical-learning orbits at deletion sizes one through nine are $1,0,0,0,1,3,7,5,7$. Every hit through nine deletions belongs to one of the proved parametric continuation families in the database; there is no unclassified hit through that cutoff. This is a finite census, not a classification at ten deletions or in higher dimension.
proof: The verifier enumerates every orbit under coordinate permutations and simultaneous complement, asserts that orbit sizes sum to the labelled count, and tests exact endpoint holes, contraction-repair sets, well-gradedness, and existence of a valid root before matching proved parametric families. The symbolic all-dimensional claims come from the individual obstruction theorems rather than extrapolation from the computation.
comments: Verified by papers/learning-spaces/scripts/explore_learning_space_pc_minors.py --max-dimension 0 --dimension-five-small-deletion-audit 9 in the preserved PartialCubes source repository. The next deletion layer alone has $\binom{30}{10}=30{,}045{,}015$ labelled sets.
